paper.title: A Systematic Literature Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Techniques, Metrics, and Challenges

evidence.paraphrase: PRISMA systematic review of 128 RAG studies covering techniques, datasets and evaluation metrics.
Recommends provenance-aware pipelines with traceable evidence, and notes LLM suggestions were advisory only in its own screening.
Its subject is generic RAG for text generation, which the frozen exclusion covers unless bibliographic curation or provenance is central.

reviews.rationale: Provenance appears only as a recommendation and the review's subject is generic RAG rather than human-controlled literature curation. It is too generic for the human_curation_governance role, though its provenance and advisory-LLM remarks make it a boundary case.

paper.title: Human-LLM Compound System for Scientific Ideation through Facet Recombination and Novelty Evaluation

evidence.paraphrase: Scideator keeps a human in the loop: users select facets from retrieved papers, and the system surfaces analogous papers at controlled semantic distances.
Includes a retrieve-then-rerank novelty checker over scholarly papers, evaluated in a user study with computer-science researchers and ablations.
The goal is idea generation rather than building or governing a bibliography.

reviews.rationale: The system is an interactive, human-controlled scholarly retrieval workflow with explicit user selection over recommended papers, which supports the human-in-the-loop part of the role. Its purpose is ideation rather than curation governance, so the fit is partial but still useful evidence.

paper.title: Human-centred learning analytics and AI in education: A systematic literature review

evidence.paraphrase: Systematic review of 108 papers on human-centred learning analytics and AI in education.
Examines the balance between human control and automation and stakeholder involvement, but for educational systems, not literature curation.

reviews.rationale: Human control versus automation is the relevant theme, but the systems are educational analytics tools with no scholarly-recommendation or evidence-selection workflow. It is out of scope, at most a conceptual analogue.

paper.title: Context-Aware Recommender Systems in the Music Domain: A Systematic Literature Review

evidence.paraphrase: Systematic review of context-aware music recommender systems using device and sensor context.
A generic consumer recommender without a scholarly or evidence-selection workflow, which the frozen boundary excludes.

reviews.rationale: Music recommendation with contextual signals has no human-curation, provenance or scholarly evidence-selection component. Out of scope under the generic-recommender exclusion.

paper.title: Explainability and Interpretability in Concept and Data Drift: A Systematic Literature Review

evidence.paraphrase: Systematic review of explainable and interpretable ML under concept and data drift.
Explainability concerns general ML model predictions, not explainable literature selection or curation.

reviews.rationale: General XAI-under-drift work does not address human control of literature curation or explainable scholarly recommendation. It is too generic for the role and out of scope.
